title: HCP — Set Standing Rule — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Set standing rule operation (HCP 6.3, 5.4; `POST /v2/rules` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.14): a Management Client, acting for the Context Subject or a delegate, sets a standing rule. HCP defines no request schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.4.14 and the standing rule of HCP 6.3. HCP 9.4.14 requires `operators`, `requires`, or both; the schema checks it with an `anyOf` of the two `required` clauses. The provider sets `ruleId`, `effect`, `setBy` and `createdAt`; none is taken from the request. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

operators.description: HCP `operators` (HCP 6.3, 9.4.14): the Client Operators (HCP 3.2.8) the rule applies to. A DNS domain matches every operator whose identifier's host is that domain or a subdomain of it; any other value matches one operator identifier exactly. Absent means every operator, which HCP allows only with `requires`. The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

requires.description: HCP `requires` (HCP 6.3, 9.4.14): client conformance claims (HCP 18.1). Where present, the rule denies only clients of the named operators that do not make every claim listed. The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

categories.description: HCP `categories` (HCP 6.3, 9.4.14): the categories the rule applies to. Absent means every category, held now or later. A delegate's rule must stay within the delegation's scope (HCP 6.3, 17.4). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque.

Response.title: HCP — Set Standing Rule — response payload
Response.description: The rule is set. Carries HCP's `201` result, the rule with its `ruleId` and `createdAt` (HCP 9.4.14), wrapped in `rule`. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

rule.description: The standing rule as the provider holds it (HCP 6.3, 9.4.14): the requested `operators`, `requires` and `categories`, with `ruleId`, `effect` (`deny`), `setBy` and `createdAt` set by the provider.
